**Test image observations:**
- Single mango leaf, mostly healthy green
- Small, round, reddish-brown spots scattered across the leaf surface (~2-4mm diameter)
- Spots appear as raised/blister-like structures
- No black coating, no large sunken lesions, no powdery growth, no curling/crumpling

**Analysis:**
- The small round reddish-brown spots match **Gall_Midge** — "round, blister-shaped galls (approximately 2–3 mm) that can be green, yellow, red or brown depending on age"
- Sooty_Mould (reference viewed) shows black encrustation coating large areas — not matching
- Anthracnose would have larger, darker, more irregular lesions
- Powdery_Mildew would show white powdery growth
- The spots are consistent in size, round, and distributed across the leaf — classic gall midge signature
